After the label conversion \(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1)\), \(\mathcal T_A(p,r)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\}\), the exact value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals this singleton, and \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}})\xrightarrow{P}\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\). As a separate boundary-coverage check, for \(|\mathcal W|=|\mathcal Z|=3\), the explicit datum \((b^{\mathrm{bd}},a^{\mathrm{bd}},T^{\mathrm{bd}},r^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}},s^{\mathrm{bd}},p^{\mathrm{bd}})\) has \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})

body.justification: This supporting theorem validates the atlas on the exact experimental overlap and on a fully specified selected assignment-boundary datum.
body.gap: Shingaki--Kuroki (2023), Theorem 1 and equations (8)--(11), identify and estimate the full response-type vector under no selection, randomized treatment, invertible cell matrices, and determinant-ratio separation; the cited theorem does not address selected forced-zero cycle fibers.
body.consumer: Experimental users can check agreement with the published plug-in estimand, while selected-data users can verify the separate boundary certificate under the present model.
body.proof_tex:
On the stated experimental submodel, \(S=1\) almost surely implies \(m=r\), and \(X\perp(U,W,Z)\) implies \(P(U=i\mid X=x)=\pi_i\).  The cited Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}shingaki\text{-}kuroki\text{-}experimental\text{-}identification}\) says that Conditions (1)--(3) identify the four response-type probabilities and that equations (8)--(13) give a consistent plug-in estimator.  We first verify that the same observable conditions make the possibly larger design-A cycle fiber target-rigid.

Fix \(e=(x,y)\) with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\), and for a proxy category \(w\) put
\[
 \widetilde Q_{ew}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
  1&P(W=w\mid E=e)\\
  P(Z=z_1\mid E=e)&P(W=w,Z=z_1\mid E=e)
 \end{pmatrix}.                                            \tag{12}
\]
The matrix used in the cited construction differs from (12) only by positive cell-probability normalizations, so the relevant determinant has the same zero pattern.  Write
\(A_{ei}=\sum_z a_{ei}(z)\) and \(A_{ej}=\sum_z a_{ej}(z)\).  Substitution of
\(T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top}\) into (12), followed by cancellation of the two diagonal products, gives
\[
 \det(\widetilde Q_{ew})
 =\{a_{ei}(z_1)A_{ej}-A_{ei}a_{ej}(z_1)\}
   \{b_i(w)-b_j(w)\}.                                     \tag{13}
\]
The determinant-ratio separation in Condition (3) makes the scalar first factor nonzero for the cells used by the published systems, and therefore \(b_i\ne b_j\).  The ratios in (13) give the observable direction of the affine line \(\mathcal L_e\).  The nonsingular systems in equations (8)--(11), together with the cross-cell separation in Conditions (2)--(3), identify the unique intersection of the two incident affine lines for each response type; this intersection is the shared endpoint \(b_i\).  In particular every cell has rank two.

Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}two\text{-}orientation\text{-}atlas}\) is exhaustive.  Once every shared endpoint is the unique incident-line intersection just obtained, every nonempty oriented endpoint interval is a singleton.  For a coordinate \(h\) satisfying \(b_i(h)\ne b_j(h)\), the cell equation gives
\[
 a_{ei}(z)
 =v_e(z)
   \frac{c_{ez}(h)-b_j(h)}{b_i(h)-b_j(h)},
 \qquad
 c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)},
 \qquad
 a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z).                              \tag{14}
\]
Selected-table positivity makes \(v_e(z)>0\), and the separating coordinate makes the denominator in (14) nonzero.  Thus all coefficient rows, and hence \(\tau_C\), are unique throughout \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).

Under \(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1)\), response consistency and randomization give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathrm{PN}
 &=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1+\pi_2}
  =\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}
          {\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_4},\\
 \mathrm{PS}
 &=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_2+\pi_4}
  =\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}
          {\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_1+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}.
 \end{aligned}                                             \tag{15}
\]
Positive observed cells make the two denominators positive.  Equations (13)--(15), the target-preserving cycle lift, and the rank-two atlas prove
\[
 \mathcal T_A(p,r)
 =\{\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\}.              \tag{16}
\]
The exact compiler of Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}atlas\text{-}handle}\) returns this singleton.  The cited plug-in consistency and continuity of \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}\) at the positive denominators in (15) yield
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}})
 \xrightarrow{P}\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}). \tag{17}
\]

We next verify the boundary datum directly.  Each listed \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is strictly positive and sums to one.  In every cell the two displayed rows of \(a^{\mathrm{bd}}\) are nonnegative, have coordinatewise sum \((1/3,1/3,1/3)\), and are linearly independent; the two incident endpoints are distinct.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}})=2
 \quad(e\in\mathcal E).                                  \tag{18}
\]
For each \((w,z)\), at least one incident coefficient is positive and all endpoint coordinates are positive, so every entry of \(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}}\), and then every entry of \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}\), is positive.  Moreover
\[
 \sum_e s_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}
 =\frac14\left(\frac18+\frac14+\frac38+\frac12\right)
 =\frac5{16},
 \qquad
 \frac{s_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}}{5/16}
 =r_e^{\mathrm{bd}}                                      \tag{19}
\]
for every cell.  The displayed cycle point and selection law therefore satisfy the normalization in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\), proving
\(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\).

Direct substitution in the simplex gives
\[
 \mathcal L_{11}=\mathcal L_{00}
 =\{b:b(w_2)=1/5\},\qquad
 \mathcal L_{01}=\{b:b(w_1)=1/5\},\qquad
 \mathcal L_{10}=\{b:b(w_3)=1/5\}.                       \tag{20}
\]
The transverse intersections in (20) fix \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_3^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(11\), the normalized columns at \(z_1,z_3\) are \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\); since the type-\(1\) endpoint is fixed, the type-\(2\) endpoint must lie on the ray starting at \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) and pointing away from \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(00\), the corresponding normalized columns are \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\); since the type-\(4\) endpoint is fixed, the same type-\(2\) endpoint must lie on the ray starting at \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) and pointing away from \(b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  The strict order on their common line is \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\), so these two rays meet only at \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  Formula (14) then fixes every coefficient, including the four displayed zeros, and
\[
 \tau_C
 =\left(0+\frac16+\frac13,
          \frac13+\frac16+0\right)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac12\right).                          \tag{21}
\]
The rank-two atlas and target-preserving lift prove
\(\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\).

On the relative support face preserving the four zero coordinates, the exposed columns continue to identify the same endpoint rays.  Positivity of every other incident coefficient and endpoint, strict endpoint order, transversality of the other incident lines, and \(m\ne r\) are strict relative inequalities.  The displayed datum satisfies them, so the relative-open chart is nonempty; the same intersection-and-ray argument proves rigidity throughout it.  Finally, \(S=1\) almost surely would imply \(P(E\mid S=1)=P(E)\), hence \(r=m\).  Since \(r^{\mathrm{bd}}\ne m^{\mathrm{bd}}\), this selected datum lies outside the 2023 experimental conditions.
